prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

In one aspect, there is provided a method comprising: receiving consumption data comprising readings from one or more utility meters associated with a property comprising one or more devices, the one or more devices comprising one or more devices of interest; determining, in the received consumption data, one or more positive consumption variations indicative of switching on of one or more of the devices and/or one or more negative consumption variations indicative of switching off of one or more of the devices; identifying one or more events associated with the one or more devices, based on the determined variations, by matching one or more positive variations with one or more negative variations; grouping the identified one or more events into one or more blocks, each block corresponding to an occurrence of usage of a device of the property; classifying the one or more blocks into one or more predetermined clusters, the one or more predetermined clusters comprising a respective predetermined cluster associated with each device of interest of the property; and determining an occurrence and/or an absence of usage of the one or more devices of interest of the property, based on the classification into the one or more predetermined clusters.

Keywords: In one aspect,

outputs.L1: In one aspect, a method is provided, the method comprising: receiving consumption data comprising readings from one or more utility meters associated with a property comprising one or more devices, including one or more devices of interest; determining, from the received consumption data, one or more positive consumption variations indicative of one or more devices being switched on and/or one or more negative consumption variations indicative of one or more devices being switched off; identifying one or more events associated with the one or more devices, based on the determined variations, by matching one or more positive variations with one or more negative variations; grouping the identified one or more events into one or more blocks, each block corresponding to an occurrence of usage of a device at the property; classifying the one or more blocks into one or more predetermined clusters, the predetermined clusters comprising a respective cluster associated with each device of interest at the property; and determining an occurrence and/or absence of usage of the one or more devices of interest at the property based on the classification into the one or more predetermined clusters.
outputs.L2: According to one aspect, a method includes obtaining consumption information containing measurements from at least one utility meter linked to a property having one or more devices, including one or more devices of interest. The consumption information is analyzed to detect positive changes representing activation of one or more devices and/or negative changes representing deactivation of one or more devices. Device-related events are then recognized by pairing one or more detected positive changes with one or more detected negative changes. The recognized events are organized into one or more blocks, with each block representing an instance in which a device at the property was used. These blocks are assigned to one or more predefined clusters, including a corresponding predefined cluster for each device of interest at the property. Based on those cluster assignments, the method establishes whether usage of any of the devices of interest occurred and/or did not occur.
outputs.L3:
Consumption data is collected from one or more utility meters associated with devices located at a property. The data is analyzed to detect positive and negative variations in consumption, which may indicate that a device has been switched on or off, respectively.

Device events are identified by matching each positive consumption variation with a corresponding negative variation. These matched events are then grouped into blocks, with each block representing a distinct occurrence or period of device usage.

Finally, the blocks are classified into predefined, device-specific clusters based on their consumption characteristics. This classification is used to determine whether devices of interest were used during the relevant period and, if so, to identify their occurrences of usage.
outputs.L4:
The method provides a way to identify the use of individual electrical devices from aggregate utility-meter data, without requiring a separate sensor for each device. It begins by analyzing a property’s time-series consumption measurements to detect significant changes in power demand. Positive changes are treated as potential device switch-on events, while corresponding negative changes are treated as potential switch-off events. Noise, background consumption, and minor fluctuations can be filtered out so that only changes likely to represent actual device activity are retained.

The detected on and off changes are then matched according to characteristics such as their magnitude, timing, duration, and expected device behavior. A compatible pair of changes forms a device event representing a period during which a device was operating. Because a single use of a device may contain multiple events or operating stages, related events are grouped into usage blocks. Each usage block therefore represents a complete or logically connected period of activity rather than an isolated change in consumption.

Features are extracted from each usage block. These may include power level, total energy consumed, operating duration, event sequence, variability, and the intervals between changes. The resulting feature set is compared with predefined, device-specific clusters that describe typical usage patterns for known devices. A block is assigned to the cluster that best matches its observed characteristics, subject to any applicable similarity or confidence threshold.

The classification result indicates whether a device of interest was likely used during the relevant time period. By repeating this process across the meter-data stream, the method can generate device-level information such as usage frequency, operating times, duration, and estimated energy consumption. In this way, aggregate property consumption data can be converted into useful appliance- or device-level monitoring information without direct instrumentation of every device.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent method claim for detecting whether specific devices in a property were used based on utility meter consumption data, including variation detection, on/off event matching, event grouping, clustering, and usage determination.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single broad patent claim for a non-intrusive load monitoring technique that identifies positive and negative consumption changes, pairs them into device events, groups the events into usage blocks, and classifies those blocks by appliance.
counterfactuals.output: 1. **A computer-implemented method for non-intrusive load monitoring, comprising:** receiving time-series measurements representative of aggregate electrical consumption by a plurality of electrical devices; detecting, from changes in the aggregate electrical consumption, positive consumption changes and negative consumption changes; pairing respective positive and negative consumption changes, based on at least a correspondence between magnitudes of the respective changes, to define device events representative of activation and deactivation of electrical loads; grouping temporally related device events into usage blocks; determining one or more characteristics of each usage block; and classifying each usage block as corresponding to an appliance based on the one or more characteristics, without separately measuring electrical consumption of the appliance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2
